title: Adapter runtime
summary: How one vendor payload becomes Sparkplug B inside an organization's adapter runtime. Each adapter is a generated Node-RED flow of four platform nodes: source, decoder, publisher and reporter. The top row turns the payload into validated metrics, the bottom row publishes them, and the middle row reports to the API.

boxes.label: Vendor device
boxes.detail: The device keeps the manufacturer's topics and payload format. It connects with a hardware credential that may only publish to the adapter's topic filters.

boxes.label: Tenant ingress broker
boxes.detail: A Mosquitto container with its own CA, TLS on port 8883 and dynamic security that denies everything by default. Messages are limited to 1 MiB. Topics under `$`, `spBv1.0/` and `iot-os/` are reserved.

boxes.label: Source node
boxes.sub: QoS 1, one input at a time
boxes.detail: Subscribes as `adapter-<uuid>` with a persistent session. It acknowledges a packet only after the publisher has settled it, so a busy decoder holds the backlog in the broker instead of dropping it. For a `vendor` source it connects out to the manufacturer's broker instead.

boxes.label: Decoder node
boxes.detail: Runs the revision's JavaScript `decode(input, helpers)` in a fresh QuickJS context per input: 100 ms of CPU, 16 MiB of memory, synchronous only. The worker itself is stopped after 500 ms of CPU. Input is at most 1 MiB and the decoder 64,000 characters.

boxes.label: Validate against profile
boxes.detail: A result needs a `sourceDeviceId` and 1 to 2,000 metrics. Each metric must be a reporting parameter of the adapter's device profile, with a value of that parameter's type and, if given, its unit. `observedAt` may be at most 5 minutes ahead. A decoder may return up to 500 results; each is checked alone.

boxes.label: Reporter node
boxes.detail: Posts events to the API with the tenant's runtime token. A source's first sample, poll runs and hourly outcome counts are retried until accepted. Other events are throttled and may be dropped under load.

boxes.label: API: adapter events
boxes.detail: A sample creates or refreshes the adapter's candidate for that source, up to 1,000 per adapter, with a preview of the decoded metrics. Failures are kept with a bounded excerpt of the input so a person can turn one into a test fixture.

boxes.label: Publisher: guards
boxes.detail: An observation older than the organization's retention is refused. A `messageId` already published is a duplicate: identifiers are kept 7 days, up to 100,000. A result older than the newest one from its source is flagged historical. Retained MQTT input is preview only.

boxes.label: Publisher: DBIRTH
boxes.detail: The Sparkplug device ID is `src-` plus the first 32 hex characters of the SHA-256 of `sourceDeviceId`. The publisher accumulates each source's metric set and sends a new DBIRTH when it changes, storing it in the births file first. One adapter announces at most 1,000 sources.

boxes.label: Publisher: DDATA
boxes.detail: Data is sent only for a source bound to a device. Each metric carries the properties `installation_uuid` and `adapter_revision_uuid`, and `timestamp_source: receipt` when the decoder gave no `observedAt`. The publish waits for the broker's acknowledgement and retries across reconnects.

boxes.label: Platform MQTT broker
boxes.detail: The publisher connects with the adapter gateway's credentials: group `adapters-<organization uuid>`, edge node `adapter-<adapter uuid>`. Its will is an NDEATH with the current bdSeq, which is stored in a file and goes up with every connection.

boxes.label: Runtime: provenance check
boxes.detail: For a device with an adapter binding, a metric without provenance is left out, because it was published before the installation existed. One whose installation does not match the enrollment becomes an invalid reading with a diagnostic.

steps.text: A vendor device publishes its own payload to the tenant's ingress broker. It can only publish to this adapter's topic filters.

The source node receives it at QoS 1 and wraps it as one decoder input, without acknowledging it yet. While the publisher cannot reach the platform broker it stops reading, and the ingress broker keeps the backlog.
The decoder node runs the revision's JavaScript in QuickJS inside a worker thread, with a fresh context and a 100 ms CPU budget.
The result is checked against the adapter's device profile: a source device ID, known metric names, matching types and units.
A decoder that throws, runs out of budget or returns something the profile does not allow produces a failure report with an excerpt of the input. Nothing is published for it.
Valid results reach the managed publisher, oldest observation first. It refuses observations older than retention and drops message IDs it has already published.
Every surviving result is reported as a sample. The API turns the first one from a new source into a candidate a person can activate.
The publisher derives the Sparkplug device ID from the source device ID and announces the source with a DBIRTH whenever its metric set changes.
If the source is bound to a device, the readings follow as DDATA, each metric stamped with the installation and adapter revision. An unbound source stops at its birth.
The platform broker acknowledges the publish. Only then is the message ID remembered, the input settled and the original packet acknowledged to the ingress broker.
On connect, on a rebirth request and when the host application comes online, the publisher sends NBIRTH with seq 0 and then a DBIRTH for every source in its births file.
The runtime ingests it like any Sparkplug device, and for an adapter-bound device stores only readings whose installation matches the enrollment.
